name.en-US: foxlink — Gmail and Calendar for agents

summary.en-US: Connect your Gmail and Google Calendar to the browser with your own Google OAuth client. Show your next events, read recent mail, and send an email only after you approve the exact message. Tokens stay encrypted in the browser.

description.en-US:
foxlink connects Gmail and Google Calendar to a browser add-on with OAuth. This add-on shows the foxlink library working, so developers can see it before they build an AI agent or another add-on on it.

**Who it is for:** developers who want an add-on or an AI agent to read mail and events, or to send mail with an approval, without a server of their own.

**What it does**

- Connect Google signs you in with Google to read mail and read calendar. The first send asks Google for the send scope.
- Show your next 3 events, the subjects of your 5 latest emails, or the text of the latest email.
- Send an email: the add-on shows the exact message (To, Cc, Bcc, subject, body, and attachments), and it sends only after you click Approve.
- Add an event: the add-on shows the title, times, time zone, attendees, and whether invites go out, and it adds the event only after you click Approve. By default nobody gets an invite.
- Disconnect revokes the token at Google.

**Requirements:** you need your own OAuth client ID from the Google Cloud console, with the Gmail API and the Google Calendar API turned on. The project README gives the steps. foxlink has no client ID of its own.

**What leaves the browser, and when**

- Only after you click Connect Google: the sign-in goes to Google, and the add-on gets tokens from Google with your client ID (and client secret, if you give one).
- When you click a button, the add-on asks Google's Gmail or Calendar API for that data. When you approve a message or an event, it sends that message through Gmail or adds that event through Calendar.
- Mail and events show only in the popup. foxlink has no server and sends nothing to its authors.

**Permissions**

- Identity: the Google sign-in window.
- Access to Google sign-in, token, Gmail and Calendar addresses: talk to Google's APIs.
- Web requests (blocking): add the access token to requests to Google's API hosts, so the popup never holds a token.
- Storage: your settings, and the tokens, encrypted.

The source code is MIT licensed.

version.approval_notes: The uploaded source.zip is the git tree of this release. To build: install Node 24 and pnpm 11 (corepack enable), run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm build:ext`. The output is dist-ext/. esbuild bundles extension/*.js with src/ and the foxgate and foxvault npm packages; the other files are copied unmodified. To try it without a Google account: run `pnpm e2e` in the source tree. It starts a local stand-in for Google (e2e/fake-google.mjs) and drives the add-on through connect, events, mail, send with approval and disconnect. `pnpm e2e` builds its own copy with `node scripts/build-ext.mjs --e2e`, which adds http://*.localhost/* and a local server port field for that stand-in. The release build that you review has neither. With a real Google account, you need your own OAuth client ID (README, section "Use your own Google client ID").

privacy_policy.en-US:
foxlink has no server. It sends nothing to its authors and has no analytics.

foxlink talks only to Google, and only after you act:

1. Connect Google opens Google's sign-in. foxlink sends your OAuth client ID, and the client secret if you gave one, to Google's token endpoint to get tokens.
2. When you click Show my next 3 events, Show 5 latest email subjects or Read the latest email, foxlink asks Google's Calendar or Gmail API for that data. It shows the result in the popup and keeps no copy.
3. When you approve an email or an event, foxlink sends that message through the Gmail API or adds that event through the Calendar API.
4. Disconnect asks Google to revoke the token.

The tokens stay in this browser, encrypted by foxvault. Your client ID, client secret and settings stay in the add-on's local storage. Google's privacy policy applies to the data that Google holds.
